key_insight: This paper studies when calibration actually helps mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, especially under distribution shift. The main takeaway is that calibrated experts can improve both reliability and performance, but only under certain conditions that the paper aims to characterize.
problem_solved: MoE models can achieve strong accuracy, but their confidence estimates may become unreliable when the test data differs from training data. This paper addresses the lack of clear understanding about when calibration improves MoE behavior under distribution shift.
method: Analyze calibration at the level of individual experts rather than only the full ensemble.
Study how distribution shift changes the relationship between calibration and MoE performance.
Identify conditions under which calibrated experts lead to better aggregate accuracy and uncertainty estimates.
impact: For ML practitioners, this work helps determine when calibration is worth applying to MoE systems in real-world settings where data often shifts over time. It supports building models that are not only accurate, but also more trustworthy and robust.
visual_elements: A MoE pipeline diagram showing experts, gating, and final prediction.
A side-by-side comparison of calibrated vs. uncalibrated confidence under distribution shift.
A reliability diagram or calibration curve illustrating uncertainty alignment.
A shift illustration showing training data vs. shifted test data.
paper_title: Toward Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Under Distribution Shift
paper_authors: Gina Wong, Drew Prinster, Suchi Saria, Rama Chellappa, Anqi Liu
